title: Scalar H0 and genus strata in proper flat curve families
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a flat, proper, finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], with geometric fibres of dimension at most one. Flatness and finite presentation for spaces are tested on etale scheme charts; proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. For $t\in T$ put $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$; geometric fibres use an algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. These fibres are schemes. There is a base-change-compatible open subscheme $U\subset T$ with
$$|U|=\{t:\dim X_t=1\text{ and }\kappa(t)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(X_t,\mathcal O_{X_t})\}.$$
For every $T'\to T$, factorization through $U$ is equivalent to every fibre of $f_{T'}$ having dimension one and the scalar map to its $H^0$ being an isomorphism. On $U$, $\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*\mathcal O_{X_U}$ universally, and $E=R^1f_*\mathcal O_{X_U}$ is finite locally free [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] with $h^*E\xrightarrow{\sim}R^1(f_{U'})_*\mathcal O_{X_{U'}}$ for every $h:U'\to U$. Hence for each integer $g\geq0$ the rank-$g$ locus $U_g$ is open and closed in $U$, commutes with arbitrary base change, and is characterized by the additional condition $\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^1(X_t,\mathcal O_{X_t})=g$. Here cohomology of spaces is cohomology of the structure module on the small etale site; on the scheme fibres it agrees with ordinary structure-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. For a geometrically reduced nonempty one-dimensional fibre, the scalar $H^0$ condition is equivalent to geometric connectedness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-fibre-dimension] to $f$. Its base-change clause identifies the dimension of $X_t$ with that of its geometric fibre, so it is at most one. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] each ordinary or geometric fibre is proper over its field, hence separated and of finite type. It is therefore a scheme by [lem-sfb-separated-space-dimension-one-scheme]. The field spectrum is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes the fibre Noetherian. For its structure module the comparison of [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison] identifies etale and ordinary cohomology. The vanishing theorem [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^i(X_t,\mathcal O)=0$ for $i>1$. Negative cohomology is zero by the definition of right derived cohomology of a module in degree zero. This also covers empty fibres.

source.place: Tag 0E1J (lemma-genus), fibre vanishing; schematic fibres via Tag 0ADD.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$: it has the one-generator presentation and is flat over $T$ because $f$ is flat. Thus $K=K_f(\mathcal O_X)$ is perfect, and for every $h:T'\to T$ there is the canonical unit-compatible isomorphism $Lh^*K\simeq K_{f_{T'}}(\mathcal O_{X_{T'}})$. At $h=i_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$, the target is $R\Gamma(X_{t,\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O)$, since a module sheaf on the one-point Zariski space is its module of global sections. Applying the cohomology functor gives the fibre groups used below; in particular its negative cohomology vanishes. These are consequences of the specified derived isomorphism, not an assumption that underived pullback commutes with higher direct image. The same theorem gives the derived counit $\epsilon_T^*K\simeq Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal O_X$ and exactness of $\epsilon_T^*$. Applying cohomology identifies the etale higher direct images with the associated etale module sheaves of $H^i(K)$; hence the ensuing Zariski local-free calculation proves the asserted etale statements as well.

source.place: Tag 0CTM (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), specialized to the structure module.

proof.text: Let $V=\{t:\dim X_t=1\}$. By [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-fibre-dimension], $V$ is open and closed and commutes with arbitrary base change. On $V$ every fibre is nonempty. A unital map from a field to its nonzero global-functions ring is injective: its kernel is an ideal of the field and cannot contain $1$. Consequently the scalar condition on $V$ is precisely $\dim H^0(X_t,\mathcal O)=1$. If it holds at $t$, apply [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model] to $K$ at $t$. All negative terms of the resulting finite free complex are zero and its degree-zero term has rank one. On its affine neighbourhood intersected with $V$, every residue complex therefore has degree-zero cohomology of dimension at most one, while the scalar injection gives dimension at least one. Thus the scalar condition holds throughout that neighbourhood. The set $U\subset V$ of such points is open in $T$. This is the $h^0\leq1$ semicontinuity argument of 0E6I, written using the existing minimal-complex lemma.

source.place: Tag 0E6I (lemma-pre-genus-curves), first two sentences of the proof; minimal model Tag 0BCD.

proof.text: For a point $t'$ over $t$, put $k=\kappa(t)$ and $k'=\kappa(t')$. The fibres are related by $X_{t'}=X_t\times_k k'$. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to the proper (hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated) scheme $X_t$ and the field extension $k\to k'$. Write $A=H^0(X_t,\mathcal O)$. Its canonical degree-zero base-change map is $A\otimes_k k'\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(X_{t'},\mathcal O)$, sending $a\otimes b$ to $b$ times the pullback of $a$. In particular $1\otimes b$ maps to $b\cdot1$. Under $k\otimes_k k'=k'$, the scalar map is therefore exactly the tensor extension of $k\to A$. A field extension is flat since every vector space has a basis; tensoring a linear map extends the bases of its kernel and cokernel and kills neither nonzero space. Thus the map is an isomorphism exactly when its extension is. The dimension comparison in [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-fibre-dimension] gives the same equivalence for dimension one. Hence the good-point set on $T'$ is the inverse image of $|U|$. A map factors through an open subscheme exactly when its image lies there. This proves both the universal factorization criterion and the base-change equality of the open loci.

For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change] identifies $K|_U=Lj^*K$ with $K_{f_U}(\mathcal O_{X_U})$ and identifies the scalar units. Write $u:\mathcal O_U\to K|_U$ for this unit. The fibre calculations above verify both hypotheses of [lem-sc-perfect-degree-zero-fibre-criterion]: $H^0(Li_t^*u)$ is an isomorphism at every point and all negative fibre cohomology vanishes. Therefore $\mathcal O_U\to H^0(K|_U)=f_*\mathcal O_{X_U}$ is an isomorphism, and locally $K|_U\simeq\mathcal O_U\oplus P$ with $P$ perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$. For any $h:U'\to U$, the same criterion applies to $Lh^*K$, using the canonical derived comparison of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change] and the fibre condition of Step 4. It gives the scalar isomorphism for $f_{U'}$, proving that the degree-zero assertion holds universally, even on a nonreduced base.

source.place: Tag 0E1J (lemma-genus), applying spaces-perfect lemma-proper-flat-h0 and its positive-degree perfect summand.

proof.text: On a neighbourhood carrying that decomposition, $Li_t^*P$ has zero cohomology except in degree one: positive-degree cohomology is that of $X_t$, which vanishes above one by Step 1, and the Tor-amplitude bound removes degrees below one. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model] to $P$ at $t$. At this fixed point $t$, all residue cohomology dimensions other than $d_1=g$ are zero. The cited model has term rank exactly $d_i$ on the entire neighbourhood, so after shrinking its terms are actually zero outside degree one and its sole term is $\mathcal O^{\oplus g}$, where $g=\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^1(X_t,\mathcal O)$. Thus the differential is zero as a module map, even if the base has nilpotents; no inference from a differential vanishing on residue fields is needed. Thus locally $K\simeq\mathcal O[0]\oplus\mathcal O^{\oplus g}[-1]$, and $E=H^1(K)=R^1f_*\mathcal O_{X_U}$ is finite locally free: every point has an open neighbourhood on which it is a finite direct sum of the structure module. Apply [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] on each such neighbourhood, where the rank is constant; no common rank on all of $U$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0E1J (lemma-genus), applying More on Algebra Tag 0BCD to the positive-degree summand.

proof.text: On any neighbourhood in Step 6 the ordinary and derived pullbacks of the displayed free terms coincide. The canonical map $h^*H^1(K)\to H^1(Lh^*K)$ is the identity on $h^*(\mathcal O^{\oplus g})$, as follows by taking degree-one cycles in the two-term complex with zero differential. Compose with the cohomology of the canonical derived base-change isomorphism of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change]. This composite is the usual higher-direct-image base-change map $h^*E\to R^1(f_{U'})_*\mathcal O$. It is locally an isomorphism and hence an isomorphism globally. The construction uses the canonical comparison throughout; a chosen local splitting is used only to check invertibility, not to choose the map.

source.place: Tag 0E1J (lemma-genus), final sentence, arbitrary base change after the one-degree calculation.

proof.text: On each of the trivializing neighbourhoods of Step 6, the fibre dimension of $E$ is the constant integer $g$. Consequently $U_g=\{t\in U:\operatorname{rank}E_t=g\}$ is open, and its complement is the union of the other open rank loci, so it is also closed. At every $t\in U$ the field case of Step 7 identifies $E\otimes\kappa(t)$ with $H^1(X_t,\mathcal O)$; hence this is exactly the locus in the statement. A pullback of $\mathcal O^{\oplus g}$ is $\mathcal O^{\oplus g}$, so ranks, and thus the open-and-closed subschemes $U_g$, commute with every base change. The empty base and the rank-zero case satisfy the same argument.

source.place: Tag 0E6K (lemma-pre-genus-one-piece-per-genus), decomposition by locally constant rank.

proof.text: For a geometrically reduced nonempty one-dimensional fibre, Step 1 supplies a proper scheme over its residue field. Apply [lem-pc-h0-geom-connected], whose hypotheses are exactly properness and geometric reducedness. Its equivalence identifies the canonical scalar $H^0$ isomorphism with geometric connectedness; it does not require smoothness, irreducibility or a rational point. This proves the last clause.

source.place: Tag 0E6L (lemma-geomredcon-in-h0-1), using the full criterion from varieties lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections.
